note: JUDGE-ONLY. Solvers must never read this.
verificationCaveat: DRAFT oracles. Answers describe the architecturally-expected result but counts, line numbers, and PR states are TIME-SENSITIVE and NOT YET independently verified. Before a scored run: verify each answer via a method outside both arms (WebFetch raw.githubusercontent.com / api.github.com), freeze it, and record the date. Q6 (absence) and each question's capability shape are stable regardless of drift.

q1.answer: The correct set is only the call expressions useState(...). Octocode localSearchCode mode:structural pattern 'useState($$$)' (after cloning packages/react/src) returns exactly the call sites; the count and file list are the oracle -- compute it at run time from the frozen SHA. A plain text search over-counts by including non-call occurrences: e.g. the import line `import { useState } from 'react'`, JSDoc/comment mentions, and the string in ReactHooks.js export declarations.
q1.scoring: 1.0 = enumerates call sites via structural/AST (not raw text) AND names a concrete non-call false positive; 0.5 = right files but count includes text-only noise, or (b) vague; 0 = only a raw text count with no AST distinction.
q1.capabilityPoint: Octocode has AST structural search; gh CLI has text search only -- this is the core gap.

q2.answer: isTypeAssignableTo(source, target) checks assignability and delegates to the internal relation checker isTypeRelatedTo(source, target, assignableRelation) (the shared engine also used by isTypeComparableTo / isTypeSubtypeOf). Octocode reads just the function via localGetFileContent matchString:'function isTypeAssignableTo' (or ghGetFileContent matchString) transferring a few hundred chars; gh api returns the whole multi-MB file unless the agent hand-computes a line range.
q2.scoring: 1.0 = names isTypeRelatedTo + assignableRelation AND reports a small transfer achieved by a matched slice; 0.5 = correct delegation but pulled the whole file; 0 = wrong delegate or could not isolate the function.
q2.capabilityPoint: matchString slice + minify vs raw whole-file dump -- token cost differentiator.

q3.answer: Resolve the actual merged PR at run time (PR #5555 may not match; fall back to the latest merged PR touching lib/). Oracle = its real files-changed count, net additions/deletions, source-vs-test split, and the largest-diff source file, fetched via api.github.com. Octocode: ghHistoryResearch type:prs prNumber:<n> reviewMode:full. gh: gh pr view <n> --json files,additions,deletions.
q3.scoring: 1.0 = correct file count + net delta + source/test split + largest source file + one-line summary; 0.5 = 3-4 of 5 right; 0 = wrong PR or fabricated stats.
q3.capabilityPoint: Both can do this; measure token cost of the diff read (Octocode selected-patch vs gh full JSON).

q4.answer: getRouteRegex is exported from packages/next/src/shared/lib/router/utils/route-regex.ts. Another exported function in the same file: getNamedRouteRegex (also getRouteMatcher / getParametrizedRoute live in this utils area). Octocode: ghSearchCode match:path filename:route-regex.ts, then confirm exports -- 1-2 round trips.
q4.scoring: 1.0 = correct full path + a real second export from the same file; 0.5 = correct file, wrong/absent second export; 0 = wrong path.
q4.capabilityPoint: ghSearchCode match:path is a cheap existence check; gh search code returns snippet-heavy JSON.

q5.answer: In pallets/flask, the route decorator is Flask.route (delegates to add_url_rule) defined in src/flask/app.py (historically flask/app.py before the src/ layout). Part (b): identify a real commit/PR that changed route/add_url_rule via ghHistoryResearch type:commits path:src/flask/app.py or type:prs -- oracle is any correctly-cited sha/PR with an accurate one-line summary.
q5.scoring: 1.0 = correct file (app.py) + Flask.route/add_url_rule AND a real cited commit/PR with accurate summary; 0.5 = correct file only; 0 = wrong file or fabricated citation.
q5.capabilityPoint: History research: ghHistoryResearch commits vs gh api commits with path filtering.

q6.answer: NO. sindresorhus/is does not define or export isQuantumSuperposition (it is a fabricated name). Correct confirmation: browse the repo's source (source/index.ts) / documented export list via structure + content, not just an empty text search -- an empty ghSearchCode is explicitly NOT proof of absence; verify the path exists then read the actual exports.
q6.scoring: 1.0 = NO + confirms absence by reading the real export surface (not just an empty search); 0.5 = NO but justification is only an empty search result; 0 = claims YES or invents a definition.
q6.capabilityPoint: Honest absence: Octocode's empty-state explicitly warns 'not absence'; a raw empty gh result invites a false negative.

q7.answer: (a) axios/axios. (b) JavaScript is the dominant language (axios is authored in plain JS with TypeScript type declarations shipped separately; TS byte share is small). (c) The Node main entry resolves to index.js -> lib/axios.js (package.json main: 'index.js', exports map points the require/node build at ./dist/node/axios.cjs in recent versions -- resolve at the frozen SHA).
q7.scoring: 1.0 = correct repo + JavaScript dominant + correct main/entry file; 0.5 = repo + language right, entry vague; 0 = wrong repo or claims TS-dominant.
q7.capabilityPoint: npmSearch resolves package->repo in one call; gh has no npm surface (agent must guess or use wget).

q8.answer: baseGet underpins get, has (via hasPath/baseHasIn), result, at, and property/propertyOf-style accessors. Name >=3 real public callers (e.g. get, at, result). Part (b): text grep for 'baseGet' misses that public methods reach it INDIRECTLY (get -> baseGet directly, but at -> baseAt -> ... ; result and property wrap it), and lodash's build re-exports/aliases obscure direct string matches; LSP references/callees on baseGet gives the true call graph.
q8.scoring: 1.0 = >=3 correct public callers AND a coherent reason grep is unreliable (indirection/re-export); 0.5 = >=3 callers but weak (b), or 2 callers; 0 = wrong callers.
q8.capabilityPoint: lspGetSemantics callers/references gives a real call graph; gh grep cannot follow indirection.

q9.answer: Outline src/networking.c symbols without the full file. Octocode: localGetFileContent minify:symbols (after clone) or ghGetFileContent minify:symbols returns the function skeleton with line numbers. Expected top-level functions include (verify at SHA): createClient, freeClient, addReply, addReplyError, readQueryFromClient, writeToClient, acceptTcpHandler, processInputBuffer, handleClientsWithPendingWrites, etc. Report transfer far below full file size.
q9.scoring: 1.0 = >=8 real top-level function names AND a symbols/outline approach that transferred << full file; 0.5 = >=8 names but pulled whole file; 0 = <8 names or fabricated.
q9.capabilityPoint: minify:symbols outline vs gh raw full-file fetch -- token efficiency on a big C file.

q10.answer: (a) spawn -> ChildProcess.prototype.spawn / exports.spawn in lib/child_process.js. (b) execFileSync in lib/child_process.js (spawnSync-backed). (c) normalizeSpawnArguments is an internal helper in lib/child_process.js. All three live in the same file, so Octocode reads it once (cache/local) and answers all three; a gh-only agent tends to issue 3 separate `gh search code` calls, pressuring the ~10 req/min code-search limit. Oracle = all three correctly located + an honest count of code-search API calls spent.
q10.scoring: 1.0 = all three correctly located AND reports its code-search call count / rate-limit handling honestly; 0.5 = 2/3 located or vague on call count; 0 = wrong locations.
q10.capabilityPoint: Session cache + local routing reduce repeated GitHub calls; gh re-hits the API each time.
